messages:
anya: quick note — bringing up quantized-ggml v2 on A100 across aws/gcp/azure. perf looks fine on AWS/Azure but GCP us-central p95 latency 2.4x higher. charts: https://interna.charts/reports/1723 (plots attached)

sam: can you paste the run command + env?

anya: run command:
```
./bench_runner --model qggml-v2 --batch 1 --seq 1024 --iters 500 --cuda-mem-pool enabled --quant int8
```
env: CUDA=12.2, driver=535.54.03, container runtime runc 1.1

lee: do we have kernel/firmware diffs across clouds? sometimes pcie gen/link speed drops on certain host types

anya: did an lspci + nvidia-smi dump. pasted below from GCP host (us-central):
```
lspci -vvv | grep -A20 'NVIDIA'
03:00.0 VGA compatible controller: NVIDIA Corporation A100-SXM4
	LnkSta: Speed 2.5GT/s, Width x8
```
```
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,driver_version,pstate,clocks.gr --format=csv
0, A100-SXM4-80GB, 535.54.03, P0, 1095 MHz
```

maria: whoa Speed 2.5GT/s is x1/x2 phys — that explains bandwidth bottleneck for large kv-cache ops.

sam: compare with AWS host output?

anya: AWS (us-west-2) dump:
```
lspci LnkSta: Speed 16GT/s, Width x16
nvidia-smi shows driver 535.54.03, clocks 1410 MHz
```

lee: so same driver but different PCIe link negotiated. Could be host BIOS, PCIe firmware, or platform nvlink/host interconnect config.

infra-bot: scheduled job #2147: run memcpy microbench on all three providers (params: 1GB buf, async) — ETA 12m

sam: i'll run a simple cudaMemcpy bw test now to confirm.

anya: sample memcpy result on GCP: 8.7 GB/s
sample on AWS: 121 GB/s

maria: that's consistent with gen2 vs gen4/5 differences. Also check NVLINK vs PCIe topology — A100 SXM expects NVLINK; some GCP instances present A100 PCIe but still show SXM label; mismatch possible.

lee: open support ticket with GCP infra and include lspci, dmesg, and the memcpy logs. Also ask for PCIe slot configuration and whether SR-IOV or passthrough is active.

anya: opened ticket: https://gcp.support/t/INC-7654 — included traces and perf graphs

sam: quick experiment idea: pin model to smaller kv-cache (512) and rerun to see if p95 gap shrinks — could be bandwidth-sensitive prefix caching

maria: also try CUDA 12.3 + driver 540.x as a sanity check, sometimes driver changes impact link negotiation behavior.

lee: tagging @platform-team — can someone check host firmware images for us-central A100 pool?

platform-team: received, will triage. preliminary note: two node images flagged with older PCIe microcode rollups.

anya: thanks. action items: sam run memcpy microbench + smaller kv-cache trial; maria try CUDA/driver matrix; lee follow up with platform and GCP ticket. i'll collate results here.

sam: starting microbench now, will post numbers.

ops-bot: canary deploy succeeded for qggml-v2: rollout 10% -> 50%

anya: cool, stopping rollout for us-central until we validate. :pause_button:

sam: memcpy numbers posted: aws 118 GB/s, azure 115 GB/s, gcp 9.1 GB/s. attaching logs.

maria: i'll spin a quick driver matrix later today.

lee: thanks everyone. keeping this thread as the single source. ping me if you need escalation.

anya: thanks — will update once we have driver/microcode diffs and patched node tests.
